title: Neighbouring bands and Johnny Lewis's son Bobo
summary: Bayou Boeuf band was the best of the rivals; no famous players came from them except Lewis's older son Bobo.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Now did they have any bands from the neighboring towns come in there?

Well, the buoy band would come get after us and the Zellema band would come to have, well, what do they used to call that? They used to call it a book and things like that. They used to call it a band Kunze. We'd play our little stuff, they'd play over there, they'd play over there, but that buoy band was the best.
Did they produce any men that have become famous since then?
They just stood around there, I guess, huh? That's all. That's all.
It was a man come here, I never seen him, but it was the son of this man I told you about, Johnny Lewis.

Well, he saw Lewis and David Lewis, them his two sons too. But he had an older son come here, played bass trombone. They said he's the talk of New Orleans. He used to play with this buddy of old. His name was Bobo, Bobo. Called him Bobo. But I believe, I don't know what his first name was, Lewis, but I know everybody called him Bobo. And they said he was a tuba playing man out of the world. But I never heard no talk of him here in New Orleans.
That's way back down, Buddy Bowling days, see? Mm-hmm. Yeah.
